context: Gap identified while shipping #4426: its PR body notes darwin-x86_64 and Windows binaries were not run locally and platform identity covers them only at SF 0.01.
description:
## Problem
`tpcds-platform-identity.yml` (via `scripts/tpcds_platform_identity.py`) compares base data and `dsqgen` parameters at SF 0.01 across the six bundled binaries. The web lineitem item-wrap bug appeared only in SF 1 refresh sets, so this check could not have caught it, and it still cannot catch a platform-specific refresh defect. The darwin-x86_64 and Windows binaries rebuilt in #4426 were never checked at SF 1 refresh; only darwin-arm64 and both Linux binaries were compared locally.

## Change
Add SF 1 refresh sets 1 and 2 (seed 20260709) to the manifest the workflow builds on every platform, as row counts and SHA-256 per refresh file, and compare them across platforms the same way base tables are compared. dsdgen generates one SF 1 refresh set in about 2 seconds.

## Decision gate
If adding SF 1 refresh sets pushes the workflow past its current time budget on any runner, bring the measured cost to the owner before reducing scope or changing the trigger.

## Guardrails
- Linux and macOS cells must agree; Windows cells keep their advisory status (owner decision 2026-10-04) unless the owner changes it.
- Do not loosen existing base-table or query comparisons.
- The check must fail, not skip, when a refresh file is missing.

## Verification rubric
- A manifest built with the pre-#4426 binaries shows a mismatch between darwin and Linux for `s_web_order_lineitem_1.dat` and `s_web_returns_1.dat`.
- The workflow passes on develop with the current binaries on all six runners, with Windows advisory.
